---
title: "Background & Corpus"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(DT)
library(janitor)

df <- read_csv("Computational_Musicology.csv") %>%
  clean_names()

corpus_explorer <- df %>%
  select(
    track_name,
    artist_name_s,
    genres,
    popularity,
    duration_ms,
    danceability,
    energy,
    loudness,
    speechiness,
    acousticness,
    liveness,
    valence,
    tempo,
    instrumentalness
  ) %>%
  mutate(duration = round(duration_ms / 60000, 2)) %>%
  select(-duration_ms) %>%
  rename(
    `track name` = track_name,
    `artist name(s)` = artist_name_s
  )
```

## Research Question

*Do my favorite songs share underlying patterns in Spotify audio features despite differences in genre, language, and artist?*

This project explores whether personal music preferences can be explained through measurable audio characteristics, using a playlist of my 100+ favorite tracks.

---

## The Playlist

::: {.ss-block}

<iframe style="border-radius:12px" 
src="https://open.spotify.com/embed/playlist/7EYqSyCa48m0MQiTRQZgB6" 
width="100%" height="380">
</iframe>

:::

The corpus is based on a personal Spotify playlist consisting of over 100 tracks.  
Rather than being curated by genre or artist, the playlist reflects individual listening preferences — songs that stand out as favorites over time.

---

## The Corpus

The dataset spans Dutch, English, and Spanish repertoire across rap, trap, R&B, pop, and soul.

Despite this apparent diversity in genre, language, and artist, the key question is whether these tracks share common underlying characteristics.  
This analysis focuses on identifying patterns that may explain why these songs are consistently preferred.

---

## Top Artists & Genres

The playlist contains a wide range of artists and genres, but some occur more frequently than others.

The top 5 most frequent artists are:
- The Weeknd (12 tracks)  
- Tory Lanez (6 tracks)  
- Frenna (4 tracks)  
- Sevn Alias (4 tracks)  
- Brent Faiyaz (3 tracks)  

In terms of genre, the top 3 occurring genres are:
- Rap  
- R&B  
- Drill  

At the same time, the playlist remains diverse, with many other artists and genres appearing less frequently.

The dataset includes songs in three main languages:
- English  
- Dutch  
- Spanish  

---

## Approach

This project applies computational analysis to uncover patterns within the playlist.

Key steps include:
- Extracting Spotify audio features (e.g. energy, danceability, tempo, valence)  
- Analyzing distributions of these features across all tracks  
- Identifying recurring patterns and potential clusters  
- Comparing perceived diversity with measurable similarity  

The goal is to determine whether subjective music preferences align with objective, data-driven characteristics.

---

## Assumptions

- Spotify audio features approximate perceptual musical qualities  
- Personal listening preferences reflect underlying patterns that can be quantified  
- Feature-based analysis provides deeper insight than genre labels alone
